# @altricade/react-mask-field — complete reference for LLMs and coding agents

> Input mask components for React (16.8–19), written in strict TypeScript, zero runtime dependencies.
> Exports: MaskField, useMask, PhoneInput, DateInput, TimeInput, CreditCardInput, plus their prop types.
> This file describes version 1.3.0 and later. Every example below is valid TypeScript.

## Install and import

```bash
npm install @altricade/react-mask-field
```

```tsx
import {
  MaskField,
  useMask,
  PhoneInput,
  DateInput,
  TimeInput,
  CreditCardInput,
  type CardType,
  type MaskFieldProps,
  type BeforeMaskedValueChangeFunction,
} from '@altricade/react-mask-field';
```

There is no default export, no CSS file to import, and no provider to set up.

## Core rules (read these first)

1. `onChange` receives a normal React `ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>`. `e.target` is the real `<input>`, and
   `e.target.value` is the **masked** string, e.g. `"(555) 123-4567"`. `e.target.name` works.
2. `value` / `defaultValue` may be masked **or** unmasked. `"5551234567"` and `"(555) 123-4567"` render identically.
   So storing the masked value from `onChange` and passing it back is correct.
3. `onChange` fires only when the masked value actually changes. Rejected keystrokes (a letter in a digit slot,
   typing into a full mask) do not fire it.
4. By default only typed characters are shown (`"(555) 12"`), and the mask template is the `placeholder`
   (`"(___) ___-____"`). Pass `alwaysShowMask` to render the full template with `maskChar` in empty slots.
5. To get the unmasked value, strip literals yourself (`e.target.value.replace(/\D/g, '')` for digit masks)
   or use `useMask(...).rawValue`. There is no `onRawChange` prop.
6. A format character inside a fixed prefix must be escaped with a backslash. In JS/TS strings the backslash
   itself is escaped: `mask={'+\\91 99999 99999'}`. Without the escape, the `9` becomes a digit slot.
7. All components forward `ref` to the underlying `<input>` and pass through every native input prop.
8. An empty mask (`mask=""`) disables masking; the value passes through unchanged.

## Mask syntax

| Char          | Meaning                                    |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `9`           | one digit `[0-9]`                          |
| `a`           | one letter `[A-Za-z]`                      |
| `*`           | one letter or digit `[A-Za-z0-9]`          |
| `\X`          | the character `X` as a literal             |
| anything else | a literal, inserted automatically          |

Custom format characters: `formatChars` maps a single mask character to a RegExp **source string** that is
anchored and tested against exactly one input character. Passing `formatChars` replaces the defaults entirely,
so include `'9'`, `'a'` and `'*'` yourself if you still need them.

```tsx
<MaskField mask="#hhhhhh" formatChars={{ h: '[0-9a-fA-F]' }} />          // "#ff0011"
<MaskField mask="99:99" formatChars={{ '9': '[0-9]' }} />
```

Mask examples:

- US phone `(999) 999-9999`
- Date `99/99/9999`
- Card `9999 9999 9999 9999`
- Canadian postcode `a9a 9a9`
- Licence plate `aaa-9999`
- IBAN-like `aa99 **** **** ****`

## MaskField

```tsx
function PhoneField() {
  const [phone, setPhone] = useState('');
  return (
    <MaskField
      mask="(999) 999-9999"
      name="phone"
      value={phone}
      onChange={e => setPhone(e.target.value)}
    />
  );
}
```

Uncontrolled:

```tsx
<MaskField mask="99/99/9999" defaultValue="12252023" ref={inputRef} />  // renders "12/25/2023"
```

Props (in addition to every native `<input>` prop):

| Prop                      | Type                                           | Default        | Notes                                                        |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `mask`                    | `string`                                       | required       | `''` disables masking                                        |
| `value`                   | `string \| number`                             | —              | controlled; masked or unmasked                               |
| `defaultValue`            | `string \| number`                             | —              | uncontrolled initial value                                   |
| `onChange`                | `(e: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void`   | —              | `e.target.value` is masked                                   |
| `maskChar`                | `string`                                       | `'_'`          | empty-slot char for `alwaysShowMask` and placeholder          |
| `alwaysShowMask`          | `boolean`                                      | `false`        | always render the full template                              |
| `formatChars`             | `Record<string, string>`                       | `9`, `a`, `*`  | replaces the defaults                                        |
| `beforeMaskedValueChange` | `BeforeMaskedValueChangeFunction`              | —              | see below                                                    |
| `placeholder`             | `string`                                       | mask template  | explicit placeholder wins                                    |
| `placeholderChar`         | `string`                                       | `maskChar`     | char used in the generated placeholder                       |
| `showPlaceholder`         | `boolean`                                      | `true`         | `false` = no generated placeholder                           |
| `error`                   | `boolean`                                      | `false`        | red border + `aria-invalid="true"`                           |
| `errorColor`              | `string`                                       | `'#d32f2f'`    | border and helper text colour when `error`                   |
| `helperText`              | `ReactNode`                                    | —              | rendered below; linked by `aria-describedby` if `id` is set  |
| `helperTextStyle`         | `CSSProperties`                                | —              | merged over the default helper style                         |
| `placeholderColor`        | `string`                                       | —              | **deprecated, ignored**; use CSS `::placeholder`             |

The rendered DOM is `<div style="display:flex;flex-direction:column;width:100%"><input/>[<div>helper</div>]</div>`.
`style` and `className` go to the `<input>`. When `error` is true, `errorColor` overrides any `borderColor` in `style`.

## beforeMaskedValueChange

```ts
type BeforeMaskedValueChangeFunction = (
  newState: { value: string; selection: { start: number | null; end: number | null } },
  oldState: { value: string; selection: { start: number | null; end: number | null } },
  userInput: string | null, // inserted text; null for deletions
  maskOptions: { mask: string; maskChar: string; formatChars: Record<string, string> }
) => { value: string; selection: { start: number | null; end: number | null } };
```

It runs after every edit. The returned value is masked again, so it cannot produce an invalid value. Return
`newState` unchanged to accept the edit.

```tsx
<MaskField
  mask="aaa-999"
  beforeMaskedValueChange={newState => ({ ...newState, value: newState.value.toUpperCase() })}
/>
```

Memoise the callback with `useCallback` if it closes over state. Inline callbacks are fine; they don't cause
extra work.

## useMask (build your own input)

```tsx
function PostcodeInput() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('');
  const mask = useMask({ mask: 'a9a 9a9', value });
  return (
    <input
      value={mask.maskedValue}
      placeholder={mask.placeholder}
      onKeyDown={mask.handleKeyDown}
      onChange={e => {
        mask.handleChange(e); // writes the masked value to e.target.value and positions the caret
        setValue(e.target.value);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

`useMask(options)` takes `mask` and `value` (both required), plus the optional `maskChar`, `formatChars`,
`alwaysShowMask`, `beforeMaskedValueChange`, `showPlaceholder` and `placeholderChar`.

It returns:

- `maskedValue` — the string to render
- `rawValue` — only the user-filled characters, e.g. `"5551234567"`
- `placeholder` — `string | undefined`
- `isComplete` — `boolean`, true when every slot is filled
- `handleChange(e)` — call it first in your `onChange`, then read `e.target.value`
- `handleKeyDown(e)` — wire it to `onKeyDown` so Backspace/Delete over separators go the right way
- `setInputValue(input, value)` and `setSelection(input, { start, end })`

## PhoneInput

```tsx
<PhoneInput countryCode="US" value={phone} onChange={e => setPhone(e.target.value)} />
```

| Prop          | Type                                                       | Default  |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| `countryCode` | `'US' \| 'CA' \| 'UK' \| 'AU' \| 'IN' \| 'RU' \| 'custom'` | `'RU'`   |
| `customMask`  | `string` (used with `'custom'`; falls back to US if absent) | —        |

Masks per country:

| Country | Mask                | Typing `1234567890` gives |
| ------- | ------------------- | ------------------------- |
| US, CA  | `+1 (999) 999-9999` | `+1 (123) 456-7890`       |
| UK      | `+44 99 9999 9999`  |                           |
| RU      | `+7 (999)999-9999`  |                           |
| AU      | `+61 9 9999 9999`   |                           |
| IN      | `+\91 99999 99999`  |                           |

Typed digits are never swallowed by the country prefix. The default is **RU**, so pass `countryCode` explicitly.
It sets `type="tel"`, `inputMode="tel"` and `autoComplete="tel"`, all of which you can override.

## DateInput

```tsx
<DateInput format="DD/MM/YYYY" value={date} onChange={e => setDate(e.target.value)} />
```

| Prop                   | Type                                                                            | Default        |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| `format`               | `'MM/DD/YYYY' \| 'DD/MM/YYYY' \| 'YYYY-MM-DD' \| 'MM-DD-YYYY' \| 'DD-MM-YYYY'` | `'MM/DD/YYYY'` |
| `separator`            | `'/' \| '-' \| '.'`                                                             | from `format`  |
| `enableDateValidation` | `boolean`                                                                       | `true`         |

Validation runs while typing and only on complete fields:

- Month is clamped to `01–12` (`13` → `12`, `00` → `01`).
- Day is clamped to `01` up to the length of the month (`04/31` → `04/30`).
- Feb 29 is allowed until the year is complete, then becomes 28 in non-leap years (Gregorian rules: 1900 is not a
  leap year, 2000 is).

It does not check min/max dates; do that in your own code (e.g. on blur or submit). The value is a string, not a
`Date`. There are no `minDate`/`maxDate` props.

## TimeInput

```tsx
<TimeInput format="24h" showSeconds value={time} onChange={e => setTime(e.target.value)} />
```

| Prop                   | Type             | Default |
| ---------------------- | ---------------- | ------- |
| `format`               | `'12h' \| '24h'` | `'12h'` |
| `showSeconds`          | `boolean`        | `false` |
| `separator`            | `':' \| '.'`     | `':'`   |
| `enableTimeValidation` | `boolean`        | `true`  |

Masks: 12h `99:99 am` → `"09:30 AM"`; 24h `99:99`; with seconds `99:99:99[ am]`.

- In 12h mode the user types the letters: `0930pm` → `09:30 PM`. The first letter slot accepts A/P, the second
  accepts M, and validation upper-cases them.
- Hours are clamped to `01–12` in 12h (`00` → `12`) and `00–23` in 24h. Minutes and seconds are clamped to `00–59`.
- `inputMode` is `"text"` for 12h (the user needs letters for AM/PM) and `"numeric"` for 24h.

## CreditCardInput

```tsx
const [cardType, setCardType] = useState<CardType | null>(null);
<CreditCardInput value={card} onChange={e => setCard(e.target.value)} onCardTypeChange={setCardType} />
```

| Prop               | Type                               | Default |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------- | ------- |
| `detectCardType`   | `boolean`                          | `true`  |
| `cardType`         | `CardType` (forces type and mask)  | —       |
| `onCardTypeChange` | `(type: CardType \| null) => void` | —       |

`CardType = 'visa' | 'mastercard' | 'amex' | 'discover' | 'diners' | 'jcb' | 'unionpay' | 'other'`.

Detection uses the number's prefix:

| Type         | Prefixes                    |
| ------------ | --------------------------- |
| `visa`       | 4                           |
| `mastercard` | 51–55, 22–27                |
| `amex`       | 34, 37                      |
| `discover`   | 6011, 65, 644–649, 622      |
| `diners`     | 36, 38, 300–305             |
| `jcb`        | 35                          |
| `unionpay`   | 62                          |
| `other`      | any other non-empty number  |
| `null`       | empty field                 |

Masks:

| Type         | Mask                  | Digits     |
| ------------ | --------------------- | ---------- |
| `amex`       | `9999 999999 99999`   | 15 (4-6-5) |
| `diners`     | `9999 999999 9999`    | 14 (4-6-4) |
| all others   | `9999 9999 9999 9999` | 16         |

`onCardTypeChange` fires once per actual change, including when a new controlled value arrives; it is not called
again on re-renders. When a pasted number switches the card type, the value is re-masked with the new mask before
`onChange` runs. The component does **not** run a Luhn checksum; validate it yourself if you need to.

## Recipes

### react-hook-form (use Controller — the inputs are controlled internally)

```tsx
<Controller
  name="phone"
  control={control}
  rules={{ validate: v => v.replace(/\D/g, '').length === 10 || 'Enter 10 digits' }}
  render={({ field, fieldState }) => (
    <PhoneInput
      countryCode="US"
      {...field}
      error={Boolean(fieldState.error)}
      helperText={fieldState.error?.message}
    />
  )}
/>
```

### Formik

```tsx
<MaskField mask="99/99/9999" name="dob" value={values.dob} onChange={handleChange} onBlur={handleBlur} />
```

`handleChange` reads `e.target.name`, which works because `e.target` is the real input.

### Validation state and accessibility

```tsx
<DateInput
  id="dob"
  value={dob}
  onChange={e => setDob(e.target.value)}
  error={dob.length > 0 && dob.length < 10}
  helperText="MM/DD/YYYY"
/>
```

This sets `aria-invalid` and links the helper text with `aria-describedby="dob-helper-text"`. Add a `<label htmlFor="dob">` yourself.

### Submitting unmasked digits

```ts
const digits = phone.replace(/\D/g, ''); // "+1 (555) 123-4567" -> "15551234567" (includes the country code)
```

For prefixed phone masks, drop the prefix explicitly. Or use `useMask({ mask, value }).rawValue`, which excludes
all literals: `"5551234567"`.

### Completeness check

```tsx
const { isComplete } = useMask({ mask: '9999 9999 9999 9999', value: card });
```

## Pitfalls (things models commonly get wrong)

- **Don't** write `mask="+91 99999 99999"`: the `9` in `91` becomes a digit slot. Use `mask={'+\\91 99999 99999'}`.
- **Don't** expect `onChange(value: string)`: it receives an event. Use `e.target.value`.
- **Don't** set `maxLength`: the mask already limits length, and `maxLength` blocks typing when `alwaysShowMask`
  is on.
- **Don't** use `type="number"` or `type="email"`: browsers don't support caret control on them. Use the default
  `type="text"`, or `type="tel"` (with `inputMode="numeric"`) for digits.
- **Don't** pass a `formatChars` object that omits `'9'` and then use `9` in the mask: it becomes a literal.
- **Don't** look for props that don't exist: `minDate`, `maxDate`, `CurrencyInput`, `onRawChange`, `guide`,
  `keepCharPositions`, `mask` as an array or function. These come from other mask libraries.
- `placeholderColor` is ignored. Style it with CSS: `input::placeholder { color: #999 }`.
- A controlled input whose parent ignores `onChange` keeps showing the controlled value (normal React behaviour).
- The default `countryCode` of `PhoneInput` is `'RU'`, not `'US'`.

## Behaviour details

- **Editing:**
  - Typing in the middle shifts later characters right.
  - Deleting shifts them left.
  - Backspace right after a separator deletes the character before the separator; Delete right before one
    deletes the character after it.
  - Selecting text and typing replaces the selection.
  - Paste accepts formatted or unformatted text and drops invalid characters.
- **Caret:** set after each edit; it jumps past separators once the slot before them is filled. It is only moved
  while the input has focus.
- **SSR:** safe (`useLayoutEffect` falls back to `useEffect` on the server). Output is deterministic.
- **Performance:** masks are parsed once and cached by content, so inline `formatChars` objects are fine. Each
  edit is O(mask length).
